case_text:
Vignette:
A 42-year-old woman presents with 8 hours of severe, constant epigastric pain radiating straight through to the back, rated 9/10. The pain began after a fatty meal and is associated with persistent nausea and multiple episodes of vomiting. She has a history of cholelithiasis diagnosed 6 months ago but declined elective cholecystectomy. On examination, she is lying very still with her knees drawn up. Vital signs: T 38.2C, HR 116, RR 22, BP 96/58, SpO2 96%. Abdomen is tender in the epigastrium with guarding but no rebound. Bowel sounds are diminished. Labs: lipase 2,840 U/L (normal <60), WBC 16,200/mcL, AST 210 U/L, ALT 185 U/L, total bilirubin 3.2 mg/dL, calcium 7.8 mg/dL. CT abdomen with contrast demonstrates a diffusely edematous pancreas with peripancreatic fluid collections and no evidence of necrosis. BISAP score is 3.
